Normalize missing-value codes in SRTR data

Source: R/srtr_normalize_missing.R
srtr_normalize_missing.Rd

SRTR variables record missing information in many ways: "Unknown", "Not done", "N/A", "Pending", blanks, and codes whose number differs from variable to variable. srtr_normalize_missing() recognises these codes from missing_codes, by what they mean in each variable's own format, and turns the ones you choose into NA.

Usage

srtr_normalize_missing(
  df,
  cols = NULL,
  policy = c("analysis", "strict", "tag_only"),
  actions = NULL,
  overrides = NULL,
  output = c("replace", "append"),
  reason = NULL,
  na_level = NULL,
  file_key = NULL,
  release = NULL,
  extra_codes = NULL,
  verbose = FALSE
)

Arguments

df

A data frame from an SRTR SAF file. Raw codes and labelled columns (from apply_srtr_factors()) are handled alike.

cols

Names of the columns to normalize. NULL (the default) takes every column that missing_codes covers.

policy

The set of rules to start from: "analysis" (the default), "strict" or "tag_only". See Policies.

actions

Changes to the policy by kind of missing value: a named character vector such as c(not_done = "keep", indeterminate = "na"). Names are types from missing_codes; values are "na" or "keep".

overrides

Changes for single variables: a named list with one element per column, each a vector like actions, such as list(REC_HIV_STAT = c(not_done = "keep")). These win over actions.

output

"replace" (the default) changes the columns in place. "append" leaves them as they are and adds the normalized values in new columns named with _NORM added.

reason

Which reason columns to add: "none" adds no columns; "changed" records the kind of each changed value; "all" records the kind of every recognised code, changed or not. NULL (the default) means "none", except under policy = "tag_only", where it means "all". See Reason columns.

na_level

A string, such as "Missing", to use in place of NA in the normalized factor and character columns, so that missing values form their own group in a table. It covers values that were NA already. For a factor it becomes the last level. Numeric columns keep NA. NULL (the default) leaves NA.

file_key

The dataset df comes from, such as "TX_KI". NULL uses the file_key attribute that load_srtr_file() sets. If there is none, variables are looked up by name alone, and a variable whose format differs between datasets is skipped, with a message.

release

The SAF release, as in load_srtr_file(). NULL uses the release recorded on df, or else the bundled dictionary.

extra_codes

Your own codes, for values that missing_codes does not cover: a named list with one element per column, each a named character vector giving the type of each value, such as list(MY_VAR = c("9" = "unknown")). These win over missing_codes, and apply alike to raw codes and to labelled columns. If two codes of a format share one label, both must be given the same type.

verbose

If TRUE, report how many values were changed in how many variables.

Value

df with the chosen codes replaced, and any reason columns added at the end. For factors, the levels that became NA are removed; the other levels keep their order, so the reference level does not depend on the order of the rows. Ordered factors stay ordered, and attributes such as variable labels are kept.

Details

Which kinds become NA is a judgement that depends on the analysis, so it is a choice. policy picks a sensible set in one word; actions and overrides adjust it by kind of missing value and by variable. Run srtr_missing_report() first to see what the data hold.

Policies

Kind (type)"analysis""strict""tag_only"
unknown, pending, cannot_discloseNANAkept
sas_missing (blank)NANAkept
not_done (not done, not tested)NANAkept
not_applicablekeptNAkept
indeterminatekeptNAkept
partial (such as "Yes, duration unknown")keptNAkept

  • "analysis" removes what carries no information about the patient and keeps what does: "not applicable" and "indeterminate" are findings, and a partly known answer still says yes.

  • "strict" leaves only substantive values.

  • "tag_only" changes no value and adds a reason column for each variable that holds a recognised code.

Whether "not done" is information depends on the question: a test that was not ordered can itself be informative. Use actions = c(not_done = "keep") to keep it.

Values that are already NA stay NA. Values that a format does not list are left alone.

Reason columns

Once "unknown" and "not done" have both become NA, they can no longer be told apart. reason = "changed" keeps that information: a column named after the variable with _MISS added records the kind of each value that was changed. It is NA for values that were not changed, including values that were NA already, and a variable gets the column only if one of its values changed. No reason columns are added by default, because a wide file can gain hundreds of them.

See also

srtr_missing_report(), missing_codes

Examples

# Made-up rows using TX_KI column names
df <- data.frame(
  DON_ANTI_CMV = c("P", "N", "U", "ND", "I"),
  DON_HIST_DIAB = c(1, 5, 998, 998, 2)
)

srtr_normalize_missing(df, file_key = "TX_KI")
#>   DON_ANTI_CMV DON_HIST_DIAB
#> 1            P             1
#> 2            N             5
#> 3         <NA>            NA
#> 4         <NA>            NA
#> 5            I             2

# Keep "not done" as a value
srtr_normalize_missing(
  df,
  actions = c(not_done = "keep"),
  file_key = "TX_KI"
)
#>   DON_ANTI_CMV DON_HIST_DIAB
#> 1            P             1
#> 2            N             5
#> 3         <NA>            NA
#> 4           ND            NA
#> 5            I             2

# Only substantive values, recording why each value became NA
srtr_normalize_missing(
  df,
  policy = "strict",
  reason = "changed",
  file_key = "TX_KI"
)
#>   DON_ANTI_CMV DON_HIST_DIAB DON_ANTI_CMV_MISS DON_HIST_DIAB_MISS
#> 1            P             1              <NA>               <NA>
#> 2            N            NA              <NA>            partial
#> 3         <NA>            NA           unknown            unknown
#> 4         <NA>            NA          not_done            unknown
#> 5         <NA>             2     indeterminate               <NA>
